newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Monday on short-covering, traders said.
The most actively traded May 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 3,400 yuan ($410) per tonne, rising 82 yuan. It opened at a low of 3,300.
July fell 45 yuan to 3,260, September rose 30 to 3,378, November 11 to 3,396 and the January 1998 contract nine to 3,399.
Combined volume rose to 30,400 tonnes from 29,100.
Soybeans opened mostly high and moved at high levels for most of the session, traders said.
"Investors were seen liquidating their short positions at low levels today," one trader said.
"They also continued to offset their positions in the May contract with the approach of the delivery date," he said.
The May 1997 contract will start delivery on May 20.
Traders said they expected soybeans to test the key 3,400 yuan resistance level in the next few days.
